story_type: rocket stage full-duration test fire, second attempt
hook: The first test stopped at one minute. This was the retry.
narration: Two months after a test shut down at one minute, NASA lit this Moon rocket again.
This is the Artemis One core stage, bolted into a test stand in Mississippi, in March 2021.
All four RS-25 engines ignited and pushed out one point six million pounds of thrust.
The stand sprays thousands of gallons of water into the flame trench to keep it from melting. That white cloud is steam.
This time the goal was the whole burn, exactly as long as a real launch.
Then the insulation on the engines caught fire. [short pause] The engineers had expected it.
In eight minutes the engines drank more than seven hundred thousand gallons of liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen.
outcome: All four engines ran the full eight minutes, and the stage came through in excellent condition.
title: Moon rocket test, take two
description:
On March 18, 2021, NASA fired the Artemis I Space Launch System core stage for a full eight minutes on the B-2 Test Stand at Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, two months after the first attempt stopped early.

Footage: NASA SSC video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/SSC_2021-03-18_Hot_Fire_B-roll_4_Views
